children: I was looking for Columbus, but I knew that he would not be there. Down by the shore, Port-au-Prince exposed its wounds to the sun; and Harry Truman Boulevard, once the most beautiful street of Haiti, was now a patchwork of potholes.
我在寻找哥伦布，但我知道他不会在那里。海岸边，太子港把自己的伤口暴露在阳光之下；哈里·杜鲁门大道——曾经是海地最美的街道——如今是一片坑洼拼缀而成的路面。

The boulevard was built for the bicentennial celebration of Port-au-Prince, which Truman helped finance right between his launching of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization and the start of the Korean War. Now, it looked like a war zone with no memory of the celebrations of which it had been the center. Only a few of the statues erected for the occasion remained. Its fountains had dried up under two Duvaliers. Its palm trees had shrunk as had Haiti itself.
这条大道是为太子港建城二百周年庆典而修建的，杜鲁门出资相助，时间恰好在他推动北大西洋公约组织成立与朝鲜战争爆发之间。如今，它看上去像个战区，对当年以自己为中心的种种庆典毫无记忆。当年为庆典竖立的雕像只剩寥寥几座。喷泉在两代杜瓦利埃治下干涸了。棕榈树萎缩了，一如海地本身。

I turned in front of the French Institute, a living monument to the impact of French culture on the Haitian elites, and drove toward the U.S. embassy, a center of power of a different order. Above a mountain of sandbags, a helmeted black G.I. watched nonchalantly as a crowd of half-naked boys bathed in a puddle left by yesterday’s rain. He had probably come with the occupying forces that helped restore President Jean-Bertrand Aristide to power in 1994. The story I was looking for went back to nine years earlier. I drove by.
我在法国研究所前转弯——它是法国文化对海地精英之影响的活纪念碑——驶向美国大使馆，一个属于另一种秩序的权力中心。在一座沙袋堆成的小山上方，一名戴着头盔的黑人大兵漫不经心地看着一群半裸的男孩在昨日雨水留下的水洼里洗澡。他多半是随1994年帮助让-贝特朗·阿里斯蒂德总统复位的占领部队来的。我要找的故事要追溯到九年前。我驱车经过。

I stopped the car at safe enough distance from the embassy and started a slow walk on the boulevard. On the buildings around the post office, conflicting graffittis asked the U.S. forces both to stay and to go home. I spotted a statue lying behind a fence across the street. A peddling artist stood next to it, selling paintings and crafts. I greeted the man and asked him if he knew where the statue of Christopher Columbus was.
我把车停在离大使馆足够安全的地方，开始沿着大道慢慢步行。邮局周围的建筑上，相互冲突的涂鸦既要求美军留下，又要求他们回家。我瞥见街对面一道栅栏后面躺着一尊雕像。一个摆摊卖画和工艺品的艺人站在旁边。我向那人打了个招呼，问他知不知道克里斯托弗·哥伦布的雕像在哪里。

I had vague memories of that statue. I only remembered its existence from my adolescent wanderings. The few images I could summon came from Graham Greene’s “The Comedians.” It was under the watchful eyes of Columbus that the heroes of that story, later played by Richard Burton and Elizabeth Taylor, consummated their illicit love. But the bust on the grass was no Columbus. The painter confirmed my doubts. “No,” he said, “this is a statue of Charlemagne Péralte.”
我对那尊雕像只有模糊的记忆。我只是从少年时代的四处游荡中记得它的存在。我能唤起的少数几个形象来自格雷厄姆·格林的《喜剧演员》。正是在哥伦布注视的目光下，那个故事的主人公们——后来由理查德·伯顿和伊丽莎白·泰勒扮演——成就了他们的禁忌之恋。但草地上的那尊半身像不是哥伦布。画家证实了我的怀疑。“不是，”他说，“这是夏尔马涅·佩拉尔特的雕像。”

Péralte was the leader of a nationalist army that fought the first occupation of Haiti by the United States in the 1920s. From the pictures the Marines took of him after they had crucified him on a door, I knew that he was a thin dark man. The bust on the grass was visibly that of a white male, rather stocky. “You’re sure this is Péralte?” I asked again. “Sure is Péralte,” replied the painter. I moved closer and read the inscription. The sculpture was a bust of Harry Truman.
佩拉尔特是一支民族主义军队的领袖，这支军队在1920年代抗击美国对海地的第一次占领。从海军陆战队把他架在一扇门板上示众后拍下的照片里，我知道他是个瘦削的黑人。草地上的半身像却显然是个白人男子，而且相当矮胖。“你确定这是佩拉尔特？”我又问。“确定是佩拉尔特，”画家答道。我走近前去，读了铭文。那尊雕塑是哈里·杜鲁门的半身像。

body.review: 底本写作20世纪20年代。美国对海地的第一次占领从1915年持续到1934年，佩拉尔特率部于1918年起事，1919年遇害。

children: “Where is the Columbus one?” I asked.
“哥伦布的那尊在哪里？”我问。
“I don’t know. I am not from Port-au-Prince,” replied the man. “Maybe it is the one that used to be near the water.”
“我不知道。我不是太子港人，”那人回答，“也许就是原先靠近水边的那一尊吧。”

I walked to the place he indicated. No statue was to be found. The pedestal was still there, but the sculpture itself was missing. Someone had inscribed on the cement: “Charlemagne Péralte Plaza.” Truman had become Péralte and Péralte had replaced Columbus.
我走到他指的地方。雕像遍寻不见。基座还在，雕塑本身却没了踪影。有人在水泥上刻下：“夏尔马涅·佩拉尔特广场”。杜鲁门变成了佩拉尔特，佩拉尔特取代了哥伦布。

I stood there for another half hour, asking each passerby if they knew what had happened to the Columbus statue. I knew the story: I was in Port-au-Prince when Columbus disappeared. I just wanted confirmation, a test of how public memory works and how history takes shape in a country with the lowest literacy rate on this side of the Atlantic.
我又在那里站了半个小时，逢过路人便问他们知不知道哥伦布雕像出了什么事。这个故事我是知道的：哥伦布失踪时我就在太子港。我只是想要一个确认，一次检验，看看公共记忆如何运作、历史在大西洋此岸识字率最低的国家里如何成形。

I was almost ready to give up when a young man recapped for me the events I had first heard about in 1986. In that year, at the fall of Jean-Claude Duvalier’s dictatorship, the most miserable people of Haiti’s capital had taken to the streets. They had thrown their anger at every monument that they associated with the dictatorship. A number of statues had been broken into pieces; others were simply removed from their bases. This was how Truman came to find himself on the grass.
我几乎要放弃时，一个年轻人向我复述了我1986年最早听说的那些事件。那一年，让-克洛德·杜瓦利埃的独裁统治垮台，海地首都最苦难的人们涌上街头。他们把怒火掷向每一座让他们联想到独裁统治的纪念碑。一些雕像被砸成碎片；另一些干脆被从基座上搬走。杜鲁门就是这样落到草地上的。

Columbus had a different fate, for reasons still unknown to me. Perhaps the illiterate demonstrators associated his name with colonialism. The mistake, if mistake there was, is understandable: the word “kolon” in Haitian means both Columbus and a colonist. Perhaps they associated him with the ocean from which he came. At any rate, when the angry crowd from the neighboring shanty towns rolled down the Harry Truman Boulevard, they took the statue of Columbus, removed it from its pedestal, and dumped it into the sea.
哥伦布的命运不同，其中的缘由我至今不明。也许那些不识字的示威者把他的名字同殖民主义联系在了一起。这个错误——如果算是错误的话——是可以理解的：海地克里奥尔语里的“kolon”一词既指哥伦布，也指殖民者。也许他们把他同他来时渡过的那片大洋联系起来。无论如何，当愤怒的人群从邻近的棚户区涌下哈里·杜鲁门大道时，他们搬走了哥伦布的雕像，把它从基座上卸下，扔进了大海。
